findings.summary: The trajectory strip under each trip panel carries numeric ticks (0.00, 0.25) but no axis label, so a reader cannot tell what the blue trace measures — confined current, residual, or axis position. The same omission recurs on frame-146-trip-2 and frame-137-trip-2. Adding a one-line y label naming the quantity and unit would make the strip readable without the page caption.

The filled red dot on the trajectory strip marks the trip whose panel is drawn, but no legend entry explains it, and red already carries 'bounding surface' and 'solved axis' in the same legend. A reader who has not read the drawing script cannot know what the coloured point means.

The text 'mask difference above each point' floats in the upper right of the residual pane, far from the data it describes, and the bare numerals printed above the curve (27, 40, 1, 0, 0 on frame 146; 24, 20, 9, 9, 0 on frame 137) are given no key inside the figure. The annotation reads as a stray title for data that is not in that corner. frame-137-flux-contours carries the same text.

Two legend entries are drawn in near-identical red — 'no bounding surface (read refused)' as a line and 'solved axis (outside wall)' as a marker — and a third red marker ('limiter contact') appears in frame-137's legend. One hue carries three meanings, so the legend cannot be resolved by colour alone; a distinct hue or dash for the refusal marker would separate them.

The poloidal panel occupies roughly a fifth of the canvas width while the residual pane holds ten mostly empty trips, so the field this figure exists to show is small on the page. It remains readable, but the allocation favours empty axis over the data.
